name: Question 1
problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $16{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}+4x+64y+44=0.$
worked_solution:
To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}16{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}+4x+64y+44 & =0 \\ 16{y}^{2}+64y-{x}^{2}+4x & =-44 \\ 16[{y}^{2}+4y]-[{x}^{2}-4x] & =-44 \\ 16[(y+2)^{2}-4]-[(x-2)^{2}-4] & =-44 \\ 16(y+2)^{2}-64-(x-2)^{2}+4 & =-44 \\ 16(y+2)^{2}-(x-2)^{2} & =-44+64-4 \\ 16(y+2)^{2}-(x-2)^{2} & =16 \\ \frac{16(y+2)^{2}}{16}-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16} & =\frac{16}{16} \\ (y+2)^{2}-\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

The asymptotes of a vertical hyperbola

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by 

$$
y-k=\pm \frac{a}{b}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
(h,k)=(2,-2),\,a=\sqrt{1}=1,\,b=\sqrt{16}=4.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$
\begin{aligned}y+2 & =\pm \frac{1}{4}(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

html:
Question 1
?

Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola 16y2−x2+4x+64y+44=0.

a
y−2=±2(x+2)
b
y+2=±12(x+2)
c
y+2=±14(x−2)
d
y+2=±4(x−2)
e
y−2=±4(x+2)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the x and y terms and complete the squares, as follows:

16y2−x2+4x+64y+44=016y2+64y−x2+4x=−4416[y2+4y]−[x2−4x]=−4416[(y+2)2−4]−[(x−2)2−4]=−4416(y+2)2−64−(x−2)2+4=−4416(y+2)2−(x−2)2=−44+64−416(y+2)2−(x−2)2=1616(y+2)216−(x−2)216=1616(y+2)2−(x−2)216=1

The asymptotes of a vertical hyperbola

(y−k)2a2−(x−h)2b2=1

are given by

y−k=±ab(x−h).

In our case, we have

(h,k)=(2,−2),a=1=1,b=16=4.

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

y+2=±14(x−2).
